title: Master ICT Review 2026: Legit or Scam?
description: Master ICT review: what its site claims about a $250 deposit, AI trading and a 4.6/5 rating, and what to check before you sign up.
author: Olivia Bennett
excerpt: Master ICT promotes AI trading with a $250 minimum and a 4.6/5 rating, but names no operator or regulator.
content:
Master ICT is presented as an AI-assisted trading platform with automated trades, a demo account and a $250 starting point. The page leaves out the operator, the regulator and the licence number, and its one performance figure is an unsourced 4.6/5 rating.

The name refers to ICT trading education, but the page describes an automated trading tool and offers no course details. Its table lists forex pairs only. The review describes the page's statements and notes which ones we could not corroborate.

Is Master ICT Legit? What the Claims Show

What the signals and automation do

The page says AI and machine learning generate signals and can place trades automatically, with a manual mode for users who prefer control. The claim cannot be tested from the page, which omits the strategy, the model and the risk limits.

Performance and ratings

The page refers to a high success rate and notable gains from a small deposit, but gives no return figures, time period, sample size or method. The 4.6/5 figure is presented without any source or count of reviews.

Asset coverage

The name refers to ICT trading education, but the page describes an automated trading tool and offers no course details. Its table lists forex pairs only. The list of tradable markets is not visible until after you have signed up.

Costs and Minimum Deposit

The page states a $250 minimum deposit and says there are no registration, transaction or withdrawal fees. The page does not list a fee schedule, spreads or any charges made by payment providers.

A standard minimum of 250 in the local currency applies for the purposes of this review: AUD 250 in Australia, GBP 250 in the UK and EUR 250 in the EU. The $250 figure appears without a currency, and the terms should be checked for the precise amount before any deposit.

Who Is Behind Master ICT

The page names no legal entity, company number or address. Sign-up buttons go to coinpulse.cc, which is a third-party domain, and the page does not say whether the publisher takes a commission from them.

Is Master ICT a Scam? Withdrawals and Complaints

Searches for Master ICT often ask whether it is a scam, whether withdrawals work and whether there are complaints. Withdrawal processing in about a day is claimed, but the page includes no limits, timelines or complaint procedure.

Look for complaint records and reviews from independent bodies, with their sources named, before depositing. How withdrawal requests are handled is not shown by a rating or by positive testimonials.

Before You Register: A Short Checklist

  • Find the legal company behind Master ICT and check it against your national regulator's register.
  • Insist on a written fee schedule that includes the spreads and any withdrawal charges.
  • Verifiable, dated performance data is worth asking for in place of a lone rating.
  • Make your opening deposit the smallest amount you could lose without strain, and test in demo mode beforehand.

Where the risk lies

The main risk is an unnamed operator, because a user has no clear party to hold to account. Where the page's claims do not match, the risk rises. Automatic execution changes who places the trades, but a losing trade is still a loss.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Master ICT legit?

The site makes claims about Master ICT but names no operator, regulator or licence number. Use the company registry and the regulator's register to check the business before you pay in.

What is the minimum deposit for Master ICT?

The page states a $250 amount and omits the currency. Read the terms for the amount and currency first, then decide whether to pay.

Is Master ICT regulated?

Without a named regulator or licence, the page refers to brokers that it does not identify. Look up the company that operates the service on the register kept by your national regulator.

Does Master ICT charge fees?

Fees are said to be absent, though the page lists no schedule covering spreads, withdrawals or currency conversion. Read the full terms first.

Would automated trading stop me losing money?

No. Automatic execution changes who places the trades, but a losing trade is still a loss.

Our Verdict on Master ICT

Master ICT's page makes broad claims without naming an operator, a regulator or verifiable results. Our rating reflects these gaps. A further look will be taken when the operator and its claims can be verified. Only money you could lose without it affecting your life belongs in an account like this.
